Here the branch only appears in the middle of the Specification sentence, so it isn't picked up. An `/answer` comment can't add it either, which means A needs a person to edit the issue. That is a human-provision step, and the data-provision and placeholder rules say to pass over it when an automated path exists. C breaks the issue's own "do not proceed on `main`" rule. The target test `test_security_audit_engine_ignores_ci_event_labels` isn't in this checkout at all (grep of `tests/` finds nothing), so a run on `main` would do nothing or fail. GITHUB FACTS show PR #6786 is open, its head `ai/issue-6782` exists at 64251aea3161, and the failing test lives on that head. PR #6786's own review/autofix loop already writes to that branch, and it feeds failed CI check-runs to the editor at top fix priority (`CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED`, default `true`). So the fix gets there with no human and no stacked PR.
